---
title: "Input controls"
---

`anylumino` provides portable anywidget input controls. Most controls are
Spectrum-backed anywidgets; date and time controls use browser-native inputs.
All of them can be nested inside any Lumino layout widget.

## Common controls

```python
from anylumino import (
    Button,
    Checkbox,
    Dropdown,
    IntSlider,
    ListBox,
    MultiSelect,
    ScrollBox,
    TextInput,
)

controls = ScrollBox(
    {
        "dataset": TextInput(value="Greenhouse A", description="Dataset"),
        "samples": IntSlider(value=120, min=25, max=250, description="Samples"),
        "metric": Dropdown(options=["Temperature", "Humidity", "CO2"], value="Temperature"),
        "enabled": Checkbox(value=True, description="Enabled"),
        "actions": Button(description="Apply"),
    },
    height=320,
)
```

## Control families

These controls are anylumino anywidgets and can be composed inside anylumino
layouts:

| Family | Controls |
|---|---|
| Text input | `TextInput`, `Text`, `TextArea`, `Textarea`, `PasswordInput`, `Password`, `Combobox`, `SearchInput` |
| Structured input | `TagsInput`, `ColorsInput`, `FloatsInput`, `IntsInput` |
| Selection | `Dropdown`, `RadioButtons`, `ToggleButtons`, `ListBox`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `SelectMultiple`, `SelectionSlider`, `SelectionRangeSlider` |
| Boolean and actions | `Button`, `Checkbox`, `ToggleButton`, `Switch`, `Valid`, `StatusLight`, `ClearButton`, `CloseButton`, `InfieldButton`, `PickerButton` |
| Integers | `IntSlider`, `IntegerSlider`, `IntRangeSlider`, `IntegerRangeSlider`, `IntText`, `IntegerInput`, `BoundedIntText`, `IntProgress` |
| Floats and progress | `FloatSlider`, `FloatRangeSlider`, `FloatLogSlider`, `FloatText`, `BoundedFloatText`, `FloatProgress`, `Meter`, `ProgressCircle` |
| Native date and time | `DatePicker`, `TimePicker`, `DatetimePicker` |
| Color | `ColorPicker`, `ColorHandle`, `ColorLoupe`, `OpacityCheckerboard` |
| File and media | `FileUpload`, `Image`, `Audio`, `Video` |
| Display and output | `Output`, `HTML`, `HTMLMath`, `Label`, `TextWidget`, `Badge`, `Link`, `Divider`, `Icon`, `UIIcon`, `HelpText`, `Tooltip`, `Underlay`, `SpectrumElement` |
| Layout surfaces | `FieldGroup`, `Popover`, `Tray`, `Overlay`, `DialogBox`, `Modal` |
| Playback | `Play` |

The generated [API reference](reference/index.qmd) includes one page per
control, with constructor signatures and argument details from anylumino's
control classes.

## Common arguments

Most controls accept a small application-oriented set of keyword arguments.
These are the ones used most often in anylumino layouts:

| Argument | Applies to | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | Most controls | Initial value and synced Python value. |
| `description` | Most form controls | Label shown above the control. |
| `disabled` | Most interactive controls | Prevent user edits while keeping the widget visible. |
| `continuous_update` | Text inputs and sliders | Whether Python receives updates while the user is typing or dragging. |
| `placeholder` | `TextInput`, `TextArea`, `PasswordInput`, `Combobox` | Empty-state text inside the input. |
| `options` | Selection controls | Choices for dropdowns, list boxes, radio buttons, and selection sliders. |
| `index`, `label` | Selection controls | Alternative ways to select or inspect the current option. |
| `min`, `max`, `step` | Numeric controls | Numeric bounds and increment size. |
| `readout`, `readout_format` | Sliders | Whether and how to show the current numeric value. |
| `orientation` | Sliders, progress bars, selection sliders | Horizontal or vertical display. |
| `rows` | `TextArea`, `ListBox`, `MultiSelect` | Visible row count. |
| `variant`, `quiet`, `icon`, `icon_src`, `icon_size`, `tooltip` | Buttons and toggle buttons | Spectrum appearance, Spectrum workflow icon metadata, custom icon source, and hover text. |
| `accept`, `multiple` | `FileUpload` | Accepted file types and whether multiple files are allowed. |

Icons on anylumino controls render through Spectrum workflow icons. Use
Spectrum names such as `CheckmarkCircle`, `AddContent`, `RotateRight`,
`Upload`, `InfoCircle`, or `HelpCircle`. Pass `icon_src` to render a custom
SVG/image through `sp-icon`, and `icon_size` for Spectrum icon sizing.
Anylumino action widgets accept the same icon fields, so toolbar examples can
share icon declarations with `Button` and `ToggleButton`.

The Spectrum components and bundled workflow icons are packaged with
anylumino's generated frontend bundles. Runtime notebooks do not need CDN
access. Use `icon_src` for custom local icon files or data URI icons.

## Design-system customization

Spectrum-backed controls are wrapped in `sp-theme` using
`spectrum_color="light"` and `spectrum_scale="medium"` by default. Pass
`spectrum_size` on individual controls where Spectrum supports component sizes.
Use `variant` for semantic or button variants and `quiet=True` for Spectrum's
quiet treatment.

For application-wide styling, define CSS custom properties on a notebook page,
JupyterLab theme, or parent widget. Spectrum components consume Spectrum CSS
tokens such as color, spacing, and typography variables, while anylumino adds a
small set of wrapper variables such as `--anylumino-control-gap`.

## Surfaces and display helpers

Input controls are not the only widgets you can compose. Anylumino also exposes
concrete surfaces and display helpers such as `DialogBox`, `Popover`,
`Tooltip`, `FieldGroup`, `HelpText`, `ProgressCircle`, `Icon`, and `UIIcon`.
Child-capable surfaces accept keyed child anywidgets and overlay-style widgets
provide `show()`, `hide()`, and `toggle()` methods.

Examples:

```python
from anylumino import Button, DialogBox, FieldGroup, TextInput, VBox

dialog = DialogBox(
    {
        "body": VBox(
            {
                "name": TextInput(value="Notebook", description="Name"),
                "close": Button(description="Close"),
            }
        )
    },
    title="Settings",
)

Button(description="Open", callbacks=[lambda _button: dialog.show()])
```

Use `SpectrumElement(tag, children=..., attributes=...)` for a Spectrum element
that is not covered by a concrete Python class yet.

## Date and time controls

`DatePicker`, `TimePicker`, and `DatetimePicker` are browser-native controls in
the non-Spectrum control module. They accept Python date/time objects as well as
compatible strings. Python values are serialized with `isoformat()` before they
are synced to the browser.

`TimePicker` renders a compact time input plus an anylumino popup with separate
hour and minute columns. The minute column contains all 60 minute values, so it
is suitable for notebook workflows that need exact time selection.

`DatetimePicker` renders a date input followed by the same time picker used by
`TimePicker`, keeping date and time edits visible in one control.

Examples:

```python
TextInput(value="Greenhouse A", description="Dataset", placeholder="Name")
IntSlider(value=120, min=25, max=250, step=5, description="Samples")
Dropdown(options=["Temperature", "Humidity", "CO2"], value="Temperature")
Button(description="Apply", icon="CheckmarkCircle", variant="accent")
TimePicker(value=time(9, 37), description="Start time")
DatetimePicker(value=datetime(2026, 5, 31, 9, 37), description="Scheduled")
```

## Aliases

These aliases are provided for application-style naming:

| anylumino alias | Canonical class |
|---|---|
| `TextInput` | `Text` |
| `TextArea` | `Textarea` |
| `PasswordInput` | `Password` |
| `ListBox` | `Select` |
| `MultiSelect` | `SelectMultiple` |
| `IntegerInput` | `IntText` |
| `IntegerSlider` | `IntSlider` |
| `IntegerRangeSlider` | `IntRangeSlider` |

## Accessing values

Input widgets expose their current Python-side value through the synced
`.value` trait. Read it directly after the widget has been created, and use
`observe(..., names="value")` when another widget should react to edits:

```python
dataset = TextInput(value="Greenhouse A", description="Dataset")
samples = IntSlider(value=120, min=25, max=250, description="Samples")

dataset.value
samples.value

def on_samples_change(change):
    print("new sample count", change["new"])

samples.observe(on_samples_change, names="value")
```

Selection widgets also expose `.value`; some additionally expose `.index` for
the selected option position. Button-like widgets use callbacks because a click
is an event, not a persistent value.

## Callback pattern

Controls are normal anywidget objects with traitlets, so use `observe()` for
state changes and `on_click()` for button-like activations:

```python
status = TextWidget("Ready")
dataset = TextInput(value="Greenhouse A", description="Dataset")

def on_dataset_change(change):
    status.value = f"Dataset: {change['new']}"

dataset.observe(on_dataset_change, names="value")

button = Button(description="Apply", icon="CheckmarkCircle", variant="accent")
button.on_click(lambda _button: setattr(status, "value", "Applied"))
```
